subject: BlueWave Labs - mid-contract growth: bridge/top-up + procurement constraints
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@bluewave.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: BlueWave Labs - mid-contract growth: bridge/top-up + procurement constraints

Hi Alicia,

Thanks for the call this morning — good to see the BlueWave team demo the new customer inbox workflow. As discussed, you expect a ~45% spike in token volume across November/December for the pilot and want to avoid a full-year uplift if the workstream doesn’t convert.

Quick summary of your ask:
- Temporary capacity top-up for Nov–Dec (estimated 45M extra tokens/month)
- Option to convert that top-up to a sustained annual uplift in Jan if metrics hit the agreed threshold
- Procurement requires either a PO for an amendment (no credit-card) or a one-off invoice + payment terms; legal needs an amendment rather than a new contract

I attached the usage snapshot for Sep–Oct to help size the request. Before I loop legal/procurement, can you confirm: 1) whether the Procurement team needs a specific amendment language around invoicing cadence, and 2) who will sign (Alicia vs Procurement lead)?

Plan from our side: I want to propose a short “bridge amendment” — 2-month top-up at a modest uplift discount, with an explicit conversion path and a defined metric gate. I’ll put together numbers and ping Marcus + David to confirm discount bands and margin sensitivity.

Next steps: if Procurement requires PO-first, we’ll produce an invoice route + payment schedule; if they accept amendment + DocuSign, we’ll push the DocuSign route to keep it fast.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0246

Attachments: usage_report_sep-oct.csv
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@bluewave.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Vega <cvega@bluewave.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@bluewave.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueWave Labs - mid-contract growth: bridge/top-up + procurement constraints

Thanks Neha — appreciate the recap. Quick answers:
1) Procurement requires line-item visibility (unit price, qty, start/end dates) and prefers a PO-first flow. They will not approve credit-card charges for amounts >$25k.
2) Procurement lead (Procurement Team) will issue PO and sign the amendment. I can approve commercially but cannot accept on behalf of Procurement.

Notes: if you can provide an invoice + SOW for the 2-month top-up that lists the unit token price, we can route the PO. Otherwise, DocuSign is fine for commercial approval but Procurement wants the PO attached to the DocuSign package.

We’re trying to move fast — pilot results expected mid-December. If the bridge is in place by 11/15, it helps us avoid throttling.

—Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Integrations, BlueWave Labs
alicia@bluewave.ai

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2026 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: BlueWave Labs - mid-contract growth: bridge/top-up + procurement constraints

Team — forwarding Alicia’s note. Key asks: 2-month top-up (approx 45M tokens/mo), PO-first preferred. Alicia says procurement will sign the amendment if we include line-item pricing and attach the PO to DocuSign. She can approve commercially but Procurement will sign.

Requirements for proposal:
- Line-item: top-up units (tokens), unit price, period (11/15–1/14), total amount
- Optional conversion term: if pilot passes metric gate (define gate in amendment), top-up converts to yearly uplift at agreed annual price (we need to specify discount bands)
- Payment: net-30 via PO preferred

Can David run preferred discount bands we can offer for a 2-month bridge with conversion optionality? Marcus — can you confirm whether we can offer a small service credit if we miss SLOs during the bridge (they care about throttling)? Soojin — any redlines to a two-month amendment with a conversion appendix?

I’m aiming to send a formal amendment draft + invoice by EOD Tues (11/2).

Thanks,
Neha
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: BlueWave Labs - mid-contract growth: bridge/top-up + procurement constraints

Neha — numbers below (rounded). Base assumptions pulled from usage_report_sep-oct.csv attached earlier.

Scenario: 2-month bridge (Nov15–Jan14), 45M extra tokens/month
- Unit token list price: $0.0009/token
- Total for bridge (gross): 90M * $0.0009 = $81,000

Discount options we can consider (one of):
A) 10% bridge discount, convertible to 5% permanent uplift if they convert to annual commitment by 1/31/2027
   - Bridge price: $72,900
   - Annualized if converted: price per token would be $0.000855
B) 15% bridge discount, no conversion guarantee; conversion to annual requires standard renewal cadence (sales to re-negotiate)
   - Bridge price: $68,850
C) 8% bridge discount + $5k service credit if any SLO breaches during bridge (fastest to approve internally)
   - Bridge price: $74,520

Margin impact: A) and C) give acceptable margin; B) is more aggressive but still within corridor if we price for expansion upside. Prefer A) from a revenue-risk perspective.

Also recommend we include a clear metric gate in amendment: conversion if average UPT (user prompt tokens) > X and error rate < Y for pilot period. I can model the annualized revenue impact quickly if they signal intent.

If Procurement wants invoice route, we’ll produce invoice for the bridge total and support net-30 with PO number attached.

-David
David Kim
Director, Customer Pricing
david_kim@redwood.ai
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2026 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: BlueWave Labs - mid-contract growth: bridge/top-up + procurement constraints

Legal/ops notes:
- Two-month amendment with conversion appendix is fine. We’ll add: specific start/end dates, line-item qty/price, conversion mechanism (timeline for conversion request: within 45 days after bridge end), and a metric gate clause with an attachment that defines the measurement method.
- Procurement PO: we can accept PO-first route. We need their PO # on DocuSign or on the invoice to lock payment terms. We should also add a short clause about payment dispute handling and change-of-scope process.
- SLO/service credit: we can offer up to $5k credit for missed SLOs in bridge period; any larger concession requires Director approval.

I’ve drafted a short amendment template and attached a PDF stub (proposed_amendment_v1.pdf). Suggested approach: send the amendment + DocuSign package, but include an alternative invoice for procurement to attach to their PO if they insist. That keeps legal happy and accommodates procurement workflows.

DocuSign link (draft package) — internal only: https://www.docusign.net/Signing/?t=abc123def
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/98765

Soojin
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@bluewave.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@bluewave.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: BlueWave Labs - mid-contract growth: bridge/top-up + procurement constraints

Alicia / Procurement team — attaching the amendment (proposed_amendment_v1.pdf) and a one-line invoice option per your PO-first preference.

Proposal (summary):
- Period: 2026-11-15 to 2027-01-14
- Line item: 90,000,000 tokens at $0.000855/token (10% bridge discount) — total bridge $72,900
- Conversion: BlueWave may elect to convert the bridge to an annual uplift by 2027-01-31; conversion price per token = $0.000855 (5% discount from list if converted) as described in Appendix A, subject to metric gate definitions in Appendix B.
- Payment: net-30 with PO number attached; alternative: sign DocuSign amendment and pay per normal invoicing cadence.
- Service credit: up to $5k for SLO breaches during the bridge (see section 4).

Alicia — can you confirm whether Procurement will attach PO to the DocuSign package or whether you prefer we issue invoice + PO #? If we don’t hear back by EOD Thursday (11/5) we’ll follow the DocuSign + attached invoice flow to avoid throttling risk.

Thanks all — I’ll update HubSpot and the DocuSign package once Alicia confirms the preferred procurement flow.

Best,
Neha

Attachments: proposed_amendment_v1.pdf, invoice_bridge_20261115.pdf
